trials.name: baseline
integer-address
trials.hypothesis: A pointer-to-integer conversion at each field base may prevent pointer reassociation while preserving 32-bit target addresses.

trials.name: element-struct
trials.hypothesis: Arrays of scalar wrappers make indexing a structure access rather than a scalar array dereference; test address lowering.

trials.name: unsigned-index
trials.hypothesis: Unsigned array indexing changes arithmetic conversion rules without changing the target ABI or valid 0..15 inputs.

trials.name: unsigned-elements
trials.hypothesis: Unsigned element comparisons and stores might change value/address expression selection; layout and equality semantics are unchanged.

trials.name: condition-local-bases
trials.hypothesis: Form the second and third field bases as assignment expressions inside short-circuit tests, preserving their conditional evaluation lifetime.

trials.name: early-return-scoped-bases
trials.hypothesis: An early-return cascade with block-scoped array bases may preserve individual address formation through expression lowering.

trials.name: inline-field-accessors
trials.hypothesis: Local C inline field accessors may be expanded after address-expression optimization, retaining distinct field-base nodes.

trials.name: inline-scalar-accessors
trials.hypothesis: Pass field bases as arguments to automatically inlined scalar accessors; test whether inline argument capture blocks reassociation.

conclusion: No new variant improved on 80.52631%. Integer address conversion, scalar structure elements, unsigned index, conditional field-base assignment, early-return scopes, and both local inline accessor variants reproduced the baseline instruction sequence. Unsigned elements regressed to 75.789474%. The retained single translation unit is exactly the best source recovered from 5414dddd0433daf5200cce6353dab5f7215b2abc.
